# Descriptors
```{r}
info <- range_read(gs, sheet = "descriptor") %>%
  rename_with(~ iconv(.x, from = "UTF-8", to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT")) %>%
  rename_with(~ str_replace_all(.x, "^[^a-zA-Z0-9]+|[^a-zA-Z0-9]+$", "")) %>%
  tidyr::fill(c(abbreviatio_sp , abbreviatio_en, descriptors), .direction = "down")

# 1. Category Dictionary

info_diccionario <- info %>% dplyr::select(cat_es, cat_en) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(cat_es, cat_en) %>% 
  tidyr::separate_rows(cat_es, cat_en, sep = ";") %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(cat_es = stringr::str_trim(cat_es),
    cat_en = stringr::str_trim(cat_en)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(cat_es, .keep_all = TRUE)
info_diccionario <- info_diccionario %>%
  dplyr::mutate( cat_en = dplyr::case_when(
      cat_es == "Cafe" ~ "Brown",
      cat_es == "Marron" ~ "Dark brown",
      TRUE ~ cat_en
    )
  )

info <- info %>% dplyr::mutate(
    descriptors = dplyr::case_when(
      abbreviatio_sp == "csco" ~ "Lighter seed coat color",
      abbreviatio_sp == "cscc" ~ "Darker seed coat color",
      TRUE ~ descriptors
    )
  )

```

# Objective 1

## Study of the morphological diversity of qualitative variables in beans accessions

### Rasgos cualitativos (Na), Numero efectivo de clases(Ne), Diversidad genetica de Nei(He) y Shannon–Weaver diversity index (H′)

```{r }

# 2. Qualitative variables

qt <- quali %>% dplyr::select(
    cce, tcvmfp, pv, cva, cv, cvmf, ph, cvs,
    fs, cda, Cpe, pcs, csco, cscc
  )
vars_q <- names(qt)

labs <- info %>%
  dplyr::filter(abbreviatio_sp %in% vars_q) %>%
  dplyr::select(abbreviatio_sp, descriptors) %>%
  tibble::deframe()


# 3. Frequency of each category
resul <- qt |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = dplyr::everything(),
    names_to = "variable",
    values_to = "categoria"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(categoria)) |>
  dplyr::count(variable, categoria, name = "Na")

print(resul, n = Inf)

sum_q <- function(df, v, lab) {
  
  tb <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[v]])) %>%
    dplyr::count(.data[[v]], name = "Na") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      fi = Na / sum(Na),
      cat_es = stringr::str_trim(as.character(.data[[v]]))
    ) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      info_diccionario,
      by = "cat_es"
    )
  
  Nc <- nrow(tb)
  
  p2 <- sum(tb$fi^2)
  
  Ne <- 1 / p2
  
  He <- 1 - p2
  
# Índice de Shannon–Weaver  (+ 0 evita imprimir "-0.00" cuando H' = 0)
  Hp <- -sum(tb$fi * log(tb$fi)) + 0
  
  tb %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      `Qualitative trait` = lab,
      `Phenotypic classes observed` =
        dplyr::coalesce(cat_en, cat_es),
      Nc = Nc,
      Ne = Ne,
      He = He,
      Hp = Hp
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      `Qualitative trait`,
      `Phenotypic classes observed`,
      Na,
      fi,
      Nc,
      Ne,
      He,
      Hp
    )
}


# 6. Calculate diversity for the 14 characters

qtb <- purrr::map_dfr(
  vars_q,
  ~ sum_q(
    qt,
    v = .x,
    lab = labs[.x]
  )
)


# 4. Resumen: una fila por carácter

res <- qtb %>%
  dplyr::distinct(
    `Qualitative trait`,
    Nc,
    Ne,
    He,
    Hp
  )

# 5. Media ± error estándar

avg <- res %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Nc_m  = mean(Nc, na.rm = TRUE),
    Nc_se = sd(Nc, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sqrt(sum(!is.na(Nc))),
    
    Ne_m  = mean(Ne, na.rm = TRUE),
    Ne_se = sd(Ne, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sqrt(sum(!is.na(Ne))),
    
    He_m  = mean(He, na.rm = TRUE),
    He_se = sd(He, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sqrt(sum(!is.na(He))),
    
    Hp_m  = mean(Hp, na.rm = TRUE),
    Hp_se = sd(Hp, na.rm = TRUE) /
      sqrt(sum(!is.na(Hp)))
  )


# 9. Formato de la tabla larga

out <- qtb %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      c(fi, Nc, Ne, He, Hp),
      ~ round(., 2)
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    `H′` = Hp
  )


fmt <- out %>%
  dplyr::group_by(`Qualitative trait`) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Na = as.character(Na),
    fi = sprintf("%.2f", fi),
    
    Nc = dplyr::if_else(
      dplyr::row_number() == 1,
      as.character(as.integer(Nc)),
      ""
    ),
    
    Ne = dplyr::if_else(
      dplyr::row_number() == 1,
      sprintf("%.2f", Ne),
      ""
    ),
    
    He = dplyr::if_else(
      dplyr::row_number() == 1,
      sprintf("%.2f", He),
      ""
    ),
    
    `H′` = dplyr::if_else(
      dplyr::row_number() == 1,
      sprintf("%.2f", `H′`),
      ""
    ),
    
    `Qualitative trait` =
      dplyr::if_else(
        dplyr::row_number() == 1,
        `Qualitative trait`,
        ""
      )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()


# Fila de media ± SE

mrow <- avg %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    `Qualitative trait` = "Mean ± SE",
    `Phenotypic classes observed` = "",
    Na = "",
    fi = "",
    Nc = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", Nc_m, Nc_se),
    Ne = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", Ne_m, Ne_se),
    He = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", He_m, He_se),
    `H′` = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", Hp_m, Hp_se)
  )


Diversity <- fmt %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      c(Nc, Ne, He, `H′`),
      as.character
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(mrow)

Diversity %>%
  knitr::kable(
    caption = "Shannon–Weaver diversity index (H′) - all phenotypic classes"
  )

writexl::write_xlsx(
  Diversity,
  "files/STable-1.xlsx"
)

```

### Diversity indices with SE and 95% CI

`quali` has one row per plant/sample, so plants of the same accession are **not** independent.
The SE and 95% CI of Ne, He and H′ are therefore obtained with a **cluster bootstrap**
(accessions are resampled with replacement, 2000 replicates), which is valid whether there is one or
several observations per accession.

```{r }
#| label: diversity-boot

div_counts <- function(cnt) {
  p <- cnt / sum(cnt)
  p <- p[p > 0]
  c(Ne = 1 / sum(p^2),
    He = 1 - sum(p^2),
    Hp = -sum(p * log(p)) + 0)
}

boot_div <- function(df, v, B = 2000) {
  d   <- df %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]))
  cnt <- unclass(table(as.character(d$entry), as.character(d[[v]])))  # accession x class
  est <- div_counts(colSums(cnt))
  bs  <- t(replicate(B, div_counts(
    colSums(cnt[sample.int(nrow(cnt), replace = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]))))
  se  <- apply(bs, 2, sd)
  ci  <- apply(bs, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))
  
  tibble::tibble(
    n_obs = nrow(d), n_acc = nrow(cnt), Nc = ncol(cnt),
    Ne = est[["Ne"]], se_Ne = se[["Ne"]], Ne_lo = ci[1, "Ne"], Ne_hi = ci[2, "Ne"],
    He = est[["He"]], se_He = se[["He"]], He_lo = ci[1, "He"], He_hi = ci[2, "He"],
    Hp = est[["Hp"]], se_Hp = se[["Hp"]], Hp_lo = ci[1, "Hp"], Hp_hi = ci[2, "Hp"]
  )
}

set.seed(123)
div_tab <- purrr::map_dfr(vars_q, \(v) {
  boot_div(quali, v) %>% 
    dplyr::mutate(trait = unname(labs[v]), .before = 1)
})

se_ <- \(x) sd(x) / sqrt(length(x))

# ---- Table 1
tab1_main <- div_tab %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    `Qualitative trait` = trait,
    `n (accessions)`    = as.character(n_acc),
    Nc                  = as.character(Nc),
    Ne                  = sprintf("%.2f", Ne),
    `He ± SE`           = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", He, se_He),
    `He 95% CI`         = sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", He_lo, He_hi),
    `H′ ± SE`           = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", Hp, se_Hp),
    `H′ 95% CI`         = sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", Hp_lo, Hp_hi)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(
      `Qualitative trait` = "Mean ± SE (across traits)",
      `n (accessions)`    = "",
      Nc                  = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", mean(div_tab$Nc), se_(div_tab$Nc)),
      Ne                  = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", mean(div_tab$Ne), se_(div_tab$Ne)),
      `He ± SE`           = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", mean(div_tab$He), se_(div_tab$He)),
      `He 95% CI`         = "",
      `H′ ± SE`           = sprintf("%.2f ± %.2f", mean(div_tab$Hp), se_(div_tab$Hp)),
      `H′ 95% CI`         = ""
    )
  )

tab1_main %>% web_table(scrolly = "400px")

writexl::write_xlsx(tab1_main, "manuscript/Table-1.xlsx")
writexl::write_xlsx(div_tab,   "files/STable-2.xlsx")
```

### Genotype fitted as a fixed effect

Genotype (`geno`) was fitted as a fixed effect to obtain Best Linear Unbiased Estimators (BLUEs) for the
multivariate analyses, using the model `y ~ 0 + (1|BLOCK) + (1|CODIGO:CHECKS) + geno`. Entries were included
as individual levels of `geno`, while checks were pooled under a single level, with the identity of each
check captured separately by the `CODIGO:CHECKS` term.

```{r }

rslt <- 14:length(exp) %>% map(\(x) {
  
trait <- names(exp)[x]

exp %>% 
   tidyr::drop_na(all_of(trait))%>% 
  H2cal(trait = trait
    , gen.name = "geno"
    , rep.n = 1
    , fixed.model = ~ 0 + (1|block) + (1|rows) + (1|cols)+ (1|entry:checks) + geno
    , random.model = ~ 1 + (1|block) + (1|rows) + (1|cols)+(1|entry:checks) + (1|geno)
    , summary = TRUE
    , emmeans = FALSE 
    , plot_diag = TRUE
    , outliers.rm = FALSE
    )

})
tabsmr <- 1:length(rslt) %>% map(\(x) {
      rslt[[x]][["tabsmr"]] 
      }) %>% 
  bind_rows()

blues <- 1:length(rslt) %>% map(\(x) {
      rslt[[x]][["blues"]] %>% dplyr::select(!matches("smith.w"))
      }) %>% Reduce(function(...) merge(..., all = TRUE
                                        , by = c('geno')), .)

blups <- 1:length(rslt) %>% map(\(x) {
      rslt[[x]][["blups"]] %>% dplyr::select(!matches("smith.w"))
      }) %>% Reduce(function(...) merge(..., all = TRUE
                                        , by = c('geno')), .)

tabsmr %>% web_table(scrolly = "400px")
writexl::write_xlsx(tabsmr, "files/STable-3.xlsx")

```

## Cluster validation 

### Silhouette width, k = 2 to 10

Average silhouette width: > 0.50 reasonable structure; 0.26–0.50 weak structure (may be artificial);
< 0.25 no substantial structure (Kaufman & Rousseeuw, 1990).

```{r }
#| label: validation-silhouette

d_pc <- dist(mv$ind$coord)                       
hc_w <- hclust(d_pc, method = "ward.D2")

sil_k <- purrr::map_dfr(2:10, \(kk) {
  s <- cluster::silhouette(cutree(hc_w, kk), d_pc)
  tibble::tibble(k = kk, avg_sil = mean(s[, "sil_width"]))
})
sil_k %>% kable(digits = 3, caption = "Average silhouette width, Ward.D2 on PCA scores")

cat("k with the highest average silhouette:", sil_k$k[which.max(sil_k$avg_sil)], "\n")

sil_final <- cluster::silhouette(as.integer(clus), d_pc)
cat("k used in the manuscript =", k, "| average silhouette =", 
    round(mean(sil_final[, "sil_width"]), 3), "\n")
print(round(tapply(sil_final[, "sil_width"], clus, mean), 3))

ps1 <- ggplot2::ggplot(sil_k, ggplot2::aes(k, avg_sil)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() + ggplot2::geom_point() +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = k, linetype = 2, colour = "red") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:10) +
  ggplot2::labs(y = "Average silhouette width", x = "Number of clusters (k)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
ps2 <- factoextra::fviz_silhouette(sil_final, print.summary = FALSE) + ggplot2::theme_minimal()

sfig_sil <- plot_grid(ps1, ps2, nrow = 1, labels = "auto", rel_widths = c(0.8, 1.2))
ggsave2(plot = sfig_sil, "files/SFigure-2.jpg", units = "cm", width = 60, height = 12)
sfig_sil
```

### MANOVA of the clusters on PC1–PC3 

The clusters were built from these same PCA scores, so the test is a **descriptive check of
separation**, not an independent hypothesis test. A PERMANOVA on the original standardised traits is added as a
complement that does not rely on multivariate normality.

```{r }
#| label: validation-manova

pcs <- as.data.frame(mv$ind$coord[, 1:3])
colnames(pcs) <- c("PC1", "PC2", "PC3")
pcs$cluster <- factor(clus[rownames(pcs)])

fit <- manova(cbind(PC1, PC2, PC3) ~ cluster, data = pcs)
summary(fit, test = "Wilks")        
summary.aov(fit)                    

Zs <- scale(blues %>% tibble::column_to_rownames("geno"))
adonis2(dist(Zs) ~ cluster, data = pcs[rownames(Zs), ], permutations = 9999)
permutest(betadisper(dist(Zs), pcs[rownames(Zs), "cluster"]), permutations = 999)
```

### Bootstrap support with pvclust

```{r }
#| label: validation-pvclust

set.seed(123)
pv <- pvclust::pvclust(t(mv$ind$coord), method.hclust = "ward.D2", 
                       method.dist = "euclidean", nboot = 1000, quiet = TRUE)

plot(pv, hang = -1, cex = 0.5, cex.pv = 0.6, main = "")
pvclust::pvrect(pv, alpha = 0.95)

jpeg("files/SFigure-3.jpg", width = 32, height = 18, units = "cm", res = 300)
plot(pv, hang = -1, cex = 0.5, cex.pv = 0.6, main = "")
pvclust::pvrect(pv, alpha = 0.95)
dev.off()

cat("Nodes with AU >= 95%:", sum(pv$edges$au >= 0.95), "of", nrow(pv$edges), "\n")
cat("Nodes with AU >= 90%:", sum(pv$edges$au >= 0.90), "of", nrow(pv$edges), "\n")
str(pvclust::pvpick(pv, alpha = 0.95)$clusters)  
```

## Correlations among traits

Spearman correlations among the 17 BLUE traits: 136 pairwise tests. p-values were adjusted with the
Benjamini–Hochberg FDR procedure (q-values); 95% CIs of rho come from a bootstrap of accessions.

```{r}
# Análisis de correlación

cuanti_matrix <- blues %>% 
  dplyr::select(2:ncol(blues))

tr_vars <- names(cuanti_matrix)     

cor_df <- combn(tr_vars, 2, simplify = FALSE) %>%
  purrr::map_dfr(\(x) {
    
    test <- cor.test(
      cuanti_matrix[[x[1]]],
      cuanti_matrix[[x[2]]],
      method = "spearman",
      exact = FALSE
    )
    
    tibble(
      Trait1 = x[1],
      Trait2 = x[2],
      rho = unname(test$estimate),
      p = test$p.value
    )
  }) %>%
  mutate(
    q = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
  )

# ---- 95% bootstrap CI of rho ------------------------------------------------
boot_rho <- function(x, y, B = 2000) {
  n <- length(x)
  r <- replicate(B, {
    i <- sample.int(n, replace = TRUE)
    suppressWarnings(cor(x[i], y[i], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"))
  })
  quantile(r, c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)
}

set.seed(123)
ci_rho <- purrr::map2(cor_df$Trait1, cor_df$Trait2,
                      \(a, b) boot_rho(cuanti_matrix[[a]], cuanti_matrix[[b]]))
cor_df$rho_lo <- purrr::map_dbl(ci_rho, 1)
cor_df$rho_hi <- purrr::map_dbl(ci_rho, 2)

cor_df %>%
  arrange(q)

cor_df %>%
  summarise(
    total = n(),
    sig_p = sum(p < 0.05),
    sig_q = sum(q < 0.05),
    lost  = sum(p < 0.05 & q >= 0.05)
  )

cor_df %>%
  filter(p < 0.05, q >= 0.05) %>%
  arrange(q)

cat(sprintf("Of the %d pairwise Spearman correlations, %d were significant at p < 0.05 (unadjusted); after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, %d remained significant (q < 0.05) and %d lost significance.\n",
            nrow(cor_df), sum(cor_df$p < 0.05), sum(cor_df$q < 0.05), 
            sum(cor_df$p < 0.05 & cor_df$q >= 0.05)))

write_xlsx(cor_df %>% arrange(q), "files/STable-5.xlsx")


# ---- Figure 3: matrix of correlations with FDR-based stars -----------------

n_tr    <- length(tr_vars)
rho_mat <- q_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, n_tr, n_tr, dimnames = list(tr_vars, tr_vars))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(cor_df))) {
  a <- cor_df$Trait1[i]; b <- cor_df$Trait2[i]
  rho_mat[a, b] <- rho_mat[b, a] <- cor_df$rho[i]
  q_mat[a, b]   <- q_mat[b, a]   <- cor_df$q[i]
}
stars_q <- \(q) ifelse(q < 0.001, "***", ifelse(q < 0.01, "**", ifelse(q < 0.05, "*", "")))
col_id  <- \(x) which(vapply(cuanti_matrix, \(col) isTRUE(all.equal(col, x, check.attributes = FALSE)), logical(1)))[1]

panel_hist <- function(x, ...) {
  usr <- par("usr"); on.exit(par(usr = usr))
  par(usr = c(usr[1:2], 0, 1.5))
  h <- hist(x, plot = FALSE)
  rect(h$breaks[-length(h$breaks)], 0, h$breaks[-1], h$counts / max(h$counts), col = "red")
}
panel_lower <- function(x, y, ...) {
  points(x, y, pch = 21, cex = 0.6)
  abline(lm(y ~ x), col = "blue", lwd = 1)
}
panel_upper <- function(x, y, ...) {
  usr <- par("usr"); on.exit(par(usr = usr))
  par(usr = c(0, 1, 0, 1))
  i <- col_id(x); j <- col_id(y)
  r <- rho_mat[i, j]; q <- q_mat[i, j]
  text(0.5, 0.5, paste0(sprintf("%.2f", r), stars_q(q)), 
       cex = 0.7 + 0.6 * abs(r), col = if (q < 0.05) "black" else "grey50")
}

grid <- \() {
  pairs(cuanti_matrix, 
        lower.panel = panel_lower, upper.panel = panel_upper, diag.panel = panel_hist,
        gap = 0.3, cex.labels = 1.1,
        main = "Spearman rho; * q<0.05, ** q<0.01, *** q<0.001 (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR)")
}

pg <- grid %>% 
  plot_grid()

ggsave2(plot = pg, filename = "manuscript/Figure_4.jpg"
        , width = 30
        , height = 30
        , units = "cm")
pg
```



# Tabla 2: Presents descriptive statistics for the quantitative traits evaluated in the blues dataset. For each trait, the table reports the mean, minimum, maximum, coefficient of variation (CV%) and broad-sense heritability (H²), providing a summary of the central tendency, range, relative variability and genetic determination of the measured characteristics.

```{r, echo=FALSE}

en <- info$abbreviatio_en
des<- info$descriptors
bluesmeans <-blues 
n <- setNames(des, en)
nb <- n[names(n) %in% colnames(bluesmeans)]
original <- setNames(names(nb),nb)
bluesmeans <- bluesmeans %>% rename(!!!original)
bluesmeans


bluesmeans %>% 
  dplyr::select(c(2:18)) %>% 
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(.x < 0, na.rm = TRUE))) %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "trait", values_to = "n_negative_BLUEs") %>% 
  dplyr::filter(n_negative_BLUEs > 0)

rl <- bluesmeans %>%
  dplyr::select(c(2:18)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ifelse(.x < 0, 0, .x))) %>%
  summarise(across(
    everything(),
    list(
      Mean = ~round(mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      Min  = ~round(min(.x, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      Max  = ~round(max(.x, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      `CV(%)` = ~round(sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE) / mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 2)
    )
  )) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = c("Quantitative trait", "stat"),
    names_pattern = "^(.*)_(Mean|Min|Max|CV\\(%\\))$",   
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = stat,
    values_from = value
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(Mean:`CV(%)`, ~formatC(.x, format = "f", digits = 2))) 

# ---- Broad-sense heritability  ------------------------
h2_cols <- grep("^H2", names(tabsmr), value = TRUE)
print(h2_cols)                                           
h2_use  <- if ("H2.c" %in% h2_cols) "H2.c" else h2_cols[1]   
cat("H2 column reported in Table 2:", h2_use, "\n")

h2_tab <- tabsmr %>% 
  dplyr::left_join(map_desc, by = c("trait" = "abbreviatio_sp")) %>%

                   H2 = sprintf("%.2f", .data[[h2_use]]))

rl <- rl %>% 
  dplyr::left_join(h2_tab, by = "Quantitative trait")

rl%>% web_table()
write_xlsx(rl, "manuscript/Table-2.xlsx")
```

## Local market controls vs. accessions (Reviewer comment 25)

`CH1` and `CH2` are the two local-market controls. Their values below are **raw plot means** of the controls,
compared with the BLUEs of the accessions (the pooled BLUE of the checks was excluded from the PCA).
The controls were not part of the clustering, so their group is obtained by projecting them onto the PCA
(supplementary individuals) and assigning them to the nearest cluster centroid.

```{r }
#| label: checks

acc <- STable1 |> 
  dplyr::select(-qrcode)

# (a) Values of the controls
STable2 %>% 
  dplyr::select(entry, dplyr::any_of(c("YP", "SW", "HI", "D50F", "D90M", "NPP", "PH90M", "SD"))) %>% 
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Controls (raw means)")

# (b) Range of the accessions
acc %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of(c("YP", "SW", "HI", "D50F", "D90M")),
                                 list(mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE), 
                                      min  = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE), 
                                      max  = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))) %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("trait", "stat"), 
                      names_pattern = "^(.*)_(mean|min|max)$") %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = stat, values_from = value) %>% 
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Accessions (BLUEs)")

# (c) % of accessions above each control
purrr::map_dfr(intersect(c("YP", "SW", "HI"), names(STable2)), \(v) {
  tibble::tibble(trait = v, control = as.character(STable2$entry),
                 control_value = STable2[[v]],
                 pct_accessions_above = purrr::map_dbl(STable2[[v]], \(z) mean(acc[[v]] > z, na.rm = TRUE) * 100))
}) %>% kable(digits = 1, caption = "% of accessions with a value higher than each control")

# (d) Cluster of each control (projection onto the PCA + nearest centroid)
act_vars <- rownames(mv$var$coord)
miss_v   <- setdiff(act_vars, names(STable2))

if (length(miss_v) == 0) {
  sup_df <- as.data.frame(STable2[, act_vars])
  rownames(sup_df) <- as.character(STable2$entry)
  sup_coord <- predict(mv, newdata = sup_df)$coord
  
  cent <- aggregate(as.data.frame(mv$ind$coord), by = list(cluster = clus), FUN = mean)
  cent_m <- t(as.matrix(cent[, -1]))
  chk_cluster <- apply(sup_coord, 1, \(z) cent$cluster[which.min(colSums((cent_m - z)^2))])
  print(data.frame(control = rownames(sup_coord), nearest_cluster = chk_cluster))
} else {
  message("STable2 lacks these active PCA variables, so the controls cannot be projected: ",
          paste(miss_v, collapse = ", "))
}
```

## Identification of promising accessions (statistical input for Figure 2, Reviewer comment 24)

Reviewer comment 24 asks that the illegible 80-accession composite (Figure 2) be moved to supplementary
material as a high-resolution figure, and that the main text show only 3–4 selected promising accessions
with clear, large images. This chunk only produces the **statistical selection** of which accessions qualify
as "promising" (the input needed to decide which photos to feature); the figure itself must still be
re-composed in image-editing software using the accessions listed below.

Objective, a-priori criterion: BLUE yield per plant above the best control **and** 100-seed weight at least equal to the best control.
Adjust the thresholds to the definition used in the manuscript.

```{r }
#| label: promising

ref_ypp <- max(STable2$YP, na.rm = TRUE)
ref_sw  <- max(STable2$SW,  na.rm = TRUE)

prom <- acc %>% 
  dplyr::filter(YP > ref_ypp, SW >= ref_sw) %>% 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(YP)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(geno, dplyr::any_of(c("YP", "SW", "HI", "D50F", "D90M", "NPP")))
prom %>% kable(digits = 2, caption = "Accessions above the best control (YP) and >= best control (SW)")

idx <- acc %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(index = as.numeric(scale(YP)) + as.numeric(scale(SW)) + as.numeric(scale(HI))) %>% 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(index)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(geno, YP, SW, HI, index)
head(idx, 6) %>% kable(digits = 2, caption = "Top accessions by an equal-weight index of YP, SW and HI")
```

# Supplementary multivariate framework for mixed data (Reviewer comment 20)

Stepwise comparison of alternatives, run on the **BLUEs (17 quantitative traits) + the qualitative descriptors**:

1. standardisation: Z-score vs. Min–Max;
2. dimension reduction: PCA, MCA, FAMD and PCoA (Gower);
3. clustering: Ward, UPGMA, k-means (and PAM on Gower), choosing k with average silhouette and the Gap statistic;
4. 2D and 3D representation.

Notes: (i) Gower already rescales each trait by its range (equivalent to Min–Max), so the standardisation only affects the
Euclidean methods (PCA, k-means, Ward); (ii) the "variance explained" of PCA, MCA, FAMD and PCoA are **not directly comparable**
(different metrics), so the selection is based on the type of data (FAMD/Gower for mixed data), the silhouette and the cophenetic correlation, and
the variance explained is reported as complementary information.

```{r }
#| label: framework-data

mode_chr <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (!length(x)) NA_character_ else names(sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
}

qual_acc <- quali %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(id_geno = stringr::str_extract(entry, "\\d+$")) %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(id_geno) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(vars_q), mode_chr), .groups = "drop") %>% 
  as.data.frame()
rownames(qual_acc) <- as.character(qual_acc$id_geno)
qual_acc$id_geno <- NULL

quant_acc <- blues %>% tibble::column_to_rownames("geno")

common   <- intersect(rownames(quant_acc), rownames(qual_acc))
qual_acc <- qual_acc[common, , drop = FALSE]

qual_acc <- qual_acc[, vapply(qual_acc, \(x) dplyr::n_distinct(x, na.rm = TRUE) > 1, logical(1)), drop = FALSE]
ok       <- stats::complete.cases(qual_acc) & stats::complete.cases(quant_acc[common, ])
cat("Accessions used:", sum(ok), "of", length(common), "\n")
common   <- common[ok]

qual_f <- qual_acc[common, , drop = FALSE] %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), factor))
quant_c <- quant_acc[common, , drop = FALSE]
mix <- cbind(quant_c, qual_f)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(names(mix)))

z  <- scale(quant_c)
mm <- apply(quant_c, 2, \(x) (x - min(x)) / (max(x) - min(x)))
```

```{r }
#| label: framework-reduction

pca_z  <- PCA(as.data.frame(z),  ncp = 5, graph = FALSE)
pca_mm <- PCA(as.data.frame(mm), ncp = 5, scale.unit = FALSE, graph = FALSE)
mca    <- MCA(qual_f, ncp = 5, graph = FALSE)
famd   <- FAMD(mix, ncp = 5, graph = FALSE)
gow    <- cluster::daisy(mix, metric = "gower")
pcoa   <- cmdscale(gow, k = 5, eig = TRUE)
pos    <- pcoa$eig[pcoa$eig > 0]

eig_cum <- \(res, n) sum(res$eig[1:n, 2])
var_expl <- tibble::tibble(
  Method = c("PCA (Z-score)", "PCA (Min-Max)", "MCA (qualitative only)", "FAMD", "PCoA (Gower)"),
  `Dim 1 (%)`   = c(eig_cum(pca_z, 1), eig_cum(pca_mm, 1), eig_cum(mca, 1), eig_cum(famd, 1), pos[1] / sum(pos) * 100),
  `Dim 1-2 (%)` = c(eig_cum(pca_z, 2), eig_cum(pca_mm, 2), eig_cum(mca, 2), eig_cum(famd, 2), sum(pos[1:2]) / sum(pos) * 100),
  `Dim 1-3 (%)` = c(eig_cum(pca_z, 3), eig_cum(pca_mm, 3), eig_cum(mca, 3), eig_cum(famd, 3), sum(pos[1:3]) / sum(pos) * 100)
)
var_expl %>% kable(digits = 1, caption = "Variance explained by each ordination (not directly comparable across methods)")
```

```{r }
#| label: framework-clustering

X_famd <- famd$ind$coord
d_famd <- dist(X_famd)

eval_hc <- function(d, method, space, label, ks = 2:10) {
  hc <- hclust(d, method)
  tibble::tibble(
    space = space, method = label, k = ks,
    avg_sil = purrr::map_dbl(ks, \(kk) mean(cluster::silhouette(cutree(hc, kk), d)[, "sil_width"])),
    cophenetic = cor(d, cophenetic(hc))
  )
}
set.seed(123)
eval_km <- function(X, d, ks = 2:10) {
  tibble::tibble(
    space = "FAMD", method = "k-means", k = ks,
    avg_sil = purrr::map_dbl(ks, \(kk) mean(cluster::silhouette(kmeans(X, kk, nstart = 50)$cluster, d)[, "sil_width"])),
    cophenetic = NA_real_
  )
}
eval_pam <- function(d, ks = 2:10) {
  tibble::tibble(
    space = "Gower", method = "PAM", k = ks,
    avg_sil = purrr::map_dbl(ks, \(kk) mean(cluster::silhouette(cluster::pam(d, kk, diss = TRUE)$clustering, d)[, "sil_width"])),
    cophenetic = NA_real_
  )
}

sil_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  eval_hc(d_famd, "ward.D2", "FAMD",  "Ward"),
  eval_hc(d_famd, "average", "FAMD",  "UPGMA"),
  eval_km(X_famd, d_famd),
  eval_hc(gow,    "ward.D2", "Gower", "Ward"),
  eval_hc(gow,    "average", "Gower", "UPGMA"),
  eval_pam(gow)
)

best_by_method <- sil_all %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(space, method) %>% 
  dplyr::slice_max(avg_sil, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(avg_sil))
best_by_method %>% kable(digits = 3, caption = "Best k (highest average silhouette) for each space x method")

set.seed(123)
gap_km <- cluster::clusGap(X_famd, FUN = kmeans, K.max = 10, B = 500, nstart = 25)
gap_wd <- cluster::clusGap(X_famd, FUN = factoextra::hcut, K.max = 10, B = 500, hc_method = "ward.D2")
k_gap_km <- cluster::maxSE(gap_km$Tab[, "gap"], gap_km$Tab[, "SE.sim"], method = "firstSEmax")
k_gap_wd <- cluster::maxSE(gap_wd$Tab[, "gap"], gap_wd$Tab[, "SE.sim"], method = "firstSEmax")
cat("Gap statistic -> k (k-means):", k_gap_km, "| k (Ward):", k_gap_wd, "\n")

pl_sil <- ggplot2::ggplot(sil_all, ggplot2::aes(k, avg_sil, colour = method, linetype = space)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() + ggplot2::geom_point() +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2:10) +
  ggplot2::labs(y = "Average silhouette width", x = "k") + ggplot2::theme_minimal()
pl_gap <- factoextra::fviz_gap_stat(gap_wd) + ggplot2::labs(title = "Gap statistic (Ward, FAMD space)")
plot_grid(pl_sil, pl_gap, nrow = 1, labels = "auto")

writexl::write_xlsx(list(variance_explained = var_expl, silhouette = sil_all, best_k = best_by_method),
                    "files/STable-10.xlsx")
```
